Chapter 6: God’s Delight in His People.
You know, sometimes there’s this really quiet moment at the end of a long day. Maybe it’s a parent, just watching their child sleep. Or a teacher, seeing that lightbulb go off as a student finally gets it. Or even a friend, catching those little kindnesses that usually go unnoticed. In these moments, you feel this deep affection—not because everything’s perfect, but because of love. And honestly, that’s just a hint of how God delights in His people.
For a lot of us, it’s tough to picture ourselves as a source of joy for God. We’re surrounded by reminders of where we fall short, of the ways we just don’t quite measure up, or of times we’ve been overlooked. But if you look closely at the story God’s been telling all along, you’ll see that His pleasure in His people isn’t about perfection or constant success. It’s about belonging. It’s about being chosen—and cherished.
Think about those who feel unseen. Maybe someone who quietly helps behind the scenes, who forgives when it’s incredibly tough, or who keeps hoping, even when hope seems almost silly. Most people might walk right by, but God notices. His delight isn’t saved for the impressive or the powerful. He finds joy in the humble, the faithful—the ones who trust Him even when it’s risky or costly.
As you follow the story, you realize something beautiful: God’s pleasure in His people is anchored in His own love, not in what they achieve. Picture a parent, softly singing a lullaby over their child—that’s the kind of joy God has. And it’s not just a warm feeling. It’s an unwavering commitment. Even when His people wander off, even when they fail, His love never walks away.
It’s so easy to slip into thinking that God’s approval is something you have to earn, that His delight is fragile or somehow conditional. But the truth? It’s way better than that. God’s joy in His people is rooted in His promises, in the work of His Son, and in the transforming power of His Spirit. He sees not just who we are now, but who we’re becoming—the beauty that’s still taking shape, the story that’s still being written.
And that… changes everything. The constant search for worth, the fear of being left out, the pressure to always perform—those things start to fade away. Instead, you begin to feel this quiet confidence, this sense of security that comes from being truly loved by the One who knows it all, and still delights in you. That’s when worship turns into more than just words. It becomes a celebration—a way of saying thank you, of resting in the joy that God takes in His people.
